greek: [343] ΓΑΛΗΝΟΥ ΤΙΝΑς ΔΕΙ ΕΚΚΑΘΑΙΡΕΙΝ ΚΑΙ ΠΟΙΟΙς ΚΑΘΑΡΤΗΡΙΟΙς ΚΑΙ ΠΟΤΕ. Τοὺς ὑγιεινὰ τὰ σώματα ἔχοντας ἐργῶδες καθαίρειν· καὶ γὰρ ἰλιγγιῶσι καὶ στροφοῦνται καὶ δυσχερῶς αὐτοῖς ἡ κάθαρσις προχωρεῖ, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἔτι ταχέως ἐκλύονται. γίνεται δὲ ταῦτα πάντα τοῦ καθαρτικοῦ φαρμάκου τὸν οἰκεῖον ἕλκειν ἐφιεμένου χυμὸν, τῷ δ’ ἀπορεῖν αὐτοῦ τὸ αἷμα καὶ τὰς σάρκας συντήκοντος, ἵν’ ἐξ ἐκείνων ἕλξῃ τὸ οἰκεῖον.
rendering_1: [343] GALEN, WHOM ONE MUST PURGE, AND WITH WHAT CATHARTICS, AND WHEN. Those who have healthy bodies are troublesome to purge; for they become dizzy and suffer griping, and the purgation proceeds with difficulty in them, and in addition to this they are, moreover, quickly exhausted. All these things come about because the cathartic drug strives to draw the humour proper to it, and, being at a loss for it, melts down the blood and the flesh, in order that it may draw from these what is proper to it.
rendering_2: [343] GALEN: WHOM ONE MUST PURGE, WITH WHAT CATHARTICS, AND WHEN. It is a laborious matter to purge those who have their bodies in a healthy state; for they become dizzy and suffer gripings, the purgation proceeds with difficulty in them, and besides this they also quickly become faint. All these things happen because the cathartic drug strives to draw its proper humour, and, through lacking it, colliquates the blood and the flesh, so that it may draw from them what is proper to it.

greek: τοὺς δ’ ὑγιαίνοντας μὲν ἔτι, νοσήσοντας [344] δ’ ἂν, εἰ μὴ κενωθεῖεν, φθάνειν δεῖ κενοῦν εἰσβάλλοντος ἦρος ἤτοι διὰ φλεβοτομίας, εἰ τοῖς πληθωρικοῖς ἁλίσκονται νοσήμασιν, ἢ διὰ καθάρσεως, εἰ τοῖς κατὰ διαφθοράν. ἡμεῖς γοῦν καὶ ποδάγραν καὶ ἀρθρῖτιν ἀρχομένην καὶ μήπω περὶ τοῖς ἄρθροις εἰργασμένην πώρους ἐκ τῆς τοιαύτης κενώσεως ἐτῶν δὴ πολλῶν ἐκωλύσαμεν γίνεσθαι. κατὰ δὲ τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον ἀποπληξίαν, ἐπιληψίαν, μελαγχολίαν, ἄλλα τε τοιαῦτα χρόνια πάθη διὰ τῆς εἰρημένης κενώσεως ἐπὶ πολλῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπαύσαμεν. ἐνίοις μὲν οὖν συμφέρει τοὺς φλεγματώδεις κενοῦσθαι χυμοὺς, ἐνίοις δὲ τοὺς πικροχόλους, ἐνίοις δὲ τοὺς μελαγχολικοὺς, ἐνίοις δὲ τὸ ὀῤῥῶδες περίττωμα κατὰ τὴν τῶν εἰθισμένων αὐτοῖς γίνεσθαι παθῶν οὐσίαν. αὐτίκα καὶ μελαγχολίᾳ τις ἁλίσκεται καθ’ ἕκαστον ἔτος, εἰ μὴ καθαρθείη, καὶ καθαίρω γε αὐτὸν οὐκ ἦρος μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ φθινοπώρου. οὕτω δὲ καὶ γυναῖκα τινὰ καθ’ ἕκαστον ἔτος εἰσβάλλοντος ἦρος ὁμοίως κενῶ, καρκινώδη διάθεσιν ἐν τῷ μασθῷ ἔχουσαν, ἣν ἰασάμην ἰσχυρῶς κενώσας διὰ φαρμάκου καθαίροντος μέλαιναν χολήν.
rendering_1: Those, however, who are still healthy but would fall ill [344] if they were not evacuated, one must evacuate in advance at the onset of spring, either by phlebotomy, if they are prone to the plethoric diseases, or by purgation, if to those arising from corruption. We at any rate, by such evacuation, have for many years now prevented both podagra and arthritis that was beginning, and had not yet produced concretions (pōroi) about the joints, from developing. In the same way we have, through the aforementioned evacuation, put a stop in many people to apoplexy, epilepsy, melancholy and other such chronic affections. For some, then, it is beneficial that the phlegmatic humours be evacuated, for some the bitter-bilious, for some the melancholic, and for some the serous residue, according to the substance of the affections that customarily befall them. For example, a certain man is seized by melancholy every year unless he is purged, and I purge him not only in spring but also in autumn. So too I likewise evacuate every year at the onset of spring a certain woman who has a cancerous condition in the breast, whom I cured by evacuating her vigorously with a drug that purges black bile.
rendering_2: But those who are still healthy, yet would fall ill [344] if they were not evacuated, one must anticipate by evacuating them at the onset of spring, either through phlebotomy, if they are seized by plethoric diseases, or through purgation, if by those arising from corruption. We, at any rate, have by means of such evacuation prevented, for many years indeed, both podagra and arthritis that was beginning and had not yet produced tophi about the joints from coming about. In the same way we have put a stop to apoplexy, epilepsy, melancholy, and other such chronic affections in many people through the aforesaid evacuation. For some, then, it is beneficial that the phlegmatic humours be evacuated, for others the bitter-bilious, for others the melancholic, for others the serous residue, according to the nature of the affections that habitually occur in them. For instance, a certain man is seized by melancholy every year if he is not purged, and I purge him not only in spring but also in autumn. So too I likewise evacuate a certain woman every year at the onset of spring, who had a cancerous condition in the breast, which I cured by evacuating her strongly with a drug that purges black bile.

greek: φαίνεται γὰρ αὕτη μετὰ τὰς πέψεις, διακρίνουσά τε τοὺς ﻿ [353] χυμοὺς, ἀποθεμένη τε τὸ περιττὸν, ἐν ᾧ δὴ καιρῷ καὶ κρίσεις γίνονται. ἀλλὰ τελέως μὲν αὐτῆς κινουμένης, οὐδὲν δεῖ φαρμακείας· μετριώτερον δὲ καὶ ἀσθενέστερον ἐνεργούσης, τὸ λεῖπον αὐτοὺς χρὴ προστιθέναι φαρμακεύοντας, ἵν’ ἐξ ἀμφοῖν ἡ τοῦ λυποῦντος χυμοῦ γένηται κένωσις, ἀπωθουμένης μὲν τῆς φύσεως, ἕλκοντος δὲ τοῦ φαρμάκου. χρὴ δ’ εἰδέναι ὡς αἱ μεταῤῥύσεις ἄλλοτε εἰς ἄλλο μόριον τῶν χυμῶν ὀλιγάκις γίνονται, τὰ δὲ πλείω ἡσυχάζει καὶ μένει καθ’ ἕν τι μόριον, ἐν ᾧ καὶ πέττεται καθ’ ὅλον τοῦ νοσήματος τὸν χρόνον ἄχρι λύσεως. ὅταν οὖν μὴ μόνον ὀξὺ πάθος ᾖ, ἀλλὰ καὶ μετὰ σφοδροτάτου πυρετοῦ, εὐλαβητέον εἰς τὴν δόσιν τοῦ καθαρτικοῦ φαρμάκου, καὶ μάλισθ’ ὅταν ἀπείρως ἔχῃ τις τῆς τοῦ κάμνοντος φύσεως. ἔνιοι μέν εἰσι φύσει δυσκάθαρτοι, τινὲς δ’ ἐπὶ βραχείᾳ πόσει φαρμάκου καθαίρονται δαψιλῶς. ὅταν οὖν ὁ πυρετὸς ᾖ μὴ σφοδρὸς, ἔμπειρός τε ἦς τῆς τοῦ κάμνοντος φύσεως, ἐπὶ τὴν τοῦ φαρμάκου δόσιν ἀφίξῃ χρώμενος ἑλλεβόρῳ μέλανι ἤ τινι τῶν ὁμοιοτρόπων, ὧν ἐστι καὶ τὸ διὰ τῆς κολοκυνθίδος, ἱερὰν δ’ αὐτὴν συνήθως ὀνομάζουσιν.
rendering_1: For it is seen, after the concoctions, both separating the [353] humours and casting off the superfluity, at which very time crises also occur. But when it is moving completely, there is no need at all of medication; when, however, it acts more moderately and more weakly, we must ourselves supply what is lacking by administering drugs, so that the evacuation of the troubling humour may come about from both together, nature thrusting it out and the drug drawing it. One must know that the fluxes of the humours from one part to another at different times occur seldom; for the most part they are at rest and remain in some one part, in which they are also concocted throughout the whole time of the disease until its resolution. So when the affection is not only acute but also accompanied by a most violent fever, one must be cautious about the giving of the cathartic drug, and most of all when one is inexperienced in the nature of the patient. Some are by nature hard to purge, while some upon a small draught of a drug are purged copiously. So when the fever is not violent, and you are experienced in the nature of the patient, you will proceed to the giving of the drug, using black hellebore or one of those of similar character, among which is also the preparation made with colocynth, which they customarily call hiera.
rendering_2: For nature is seen, after the concoctions, both separating the [353] humours and setting aside the superfluity, at which time crises also occur. But when nature is moved perfectly, there is no need of purging with drugs; when it acts more moderately and more weakly, we ourselves must supply what is lacking by administering drugs, so that the evacuation of the troublesome humour may come about from both, nature thrusting it away and the drug drawing it. One must know that the shiftings of the humours, now into one part and now into another, occur rarely; for the most part they are at rest and remain in some one part, in which they are also concocted throughout the whole time of the disease until its resolution. When, therefore, the affection is not only acute but is also accompanied by a very violent fever, one must be cautious about giving the cathartic drug, and especially when one is unacquainted with the nature of the patient. Some people are by nature hard to purge, while others are purged copiously upon a small draught of the drug. When, therefore, the fever is not violent and you are acquainted with the nature of the patient, you will proceed to the giving of the drug, using black hellebore or one of those of similar character, among which is also the preparation made with colocynth; they customarily call it hiera.

greek: [354] ποικίλως δ’ αὐτῆς σκευαζομένης, ἡ τὸν ἑλλέβορον εἰληφυῖα, τὴν σκαμμωνίαν δ’ οὐκ ἔχουσα, κάλλιστόν ἐστι φάρμακον ὑπήλατον. μετὰ δὲ τὸ ληφθῆναι τὸ καθαρτήριον συμφέρει τῆς πτισάνης ἐπιῤῥοφεῖν, ὥς φησιν Ἱπποκράτης. αὐτὸ μὲν γὰρ τὸ καθαρτικὸν φάρμακον, ὡς ἂν ὀλίγον ὂν, εἰς τὸν πυθμένα τῆς κοιλίας ἀφικνεῖται, κατὰ δὲ τὴν δίοδον ὅ τε στόμαχος ὅσον περὶ τῆς γαστρὸς ὑψηλὸν, οὐ μόνον τῆς ποιότητος τοῦ καθαίροντος, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς οὐσίας προσιζούσης ἐν τῇ διόδῳ μεταλαμβάνων μεγάλως βλάπτεται. χρήσιμος οὖν ὁ χυλὸς τῆς πτισάνης ἐπιῤῥοφούμενος, ὡς ἂν ἀποῤῥῦψαι μὲν καὶ κατασῦραι κάτω τὸ προσπεπλασμένον ἐν τῇ διόδῳ δυνάμενος, ἐπικεράσαι δὲ καὶ ὑπαλλάξαι τὴν ἐνιζηκυῖαν τοῖς μορίοις ποιότητα τοῦ φαρμάκου. διὰ ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ἐπὶ τῇ τοῦ καθαρτικοῦ φαρμάκου πόσει κελεύει τῆς πτισάνης ἐπιῤῥοφεῖν. ἀρξαμένης δὲ τῆς καθάρσεως γίνεσθαι οὐκέτι βούλεται δίδοσθαι πτισάνης, εὐλαβούμενος ἐκλυθῆναι τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ καθαίροντος φαρμάκου.
rendering_1: [354] Since it is prepared in various ways, the one that has taken in hellebore but does not contain scammony is a most excellent drug for purging downwards. After the purgative has been taken, it is beneficial to sip some ptisan after it, as Hippocrates says. For the cathartic drug itself, being small in quantity, reaches the bottom of the belly. But along its passage the gullet (stomachos), and as much of the stomach as lies high up, take up not only the quality of the purging agent but also its substance, which settles in the passage, and they are greatly harmed. The juice of the ptisan, therefore, is useful when sipped afterwards. It can wash off what has stuck in the passage and sweep it downward, and it can temper and alter the quality of the drug that has settled in the parts. For these reasons, then, he bids one sip ptisan after the drinking of the cathartic drug. But once the purgation has begun to take place, he no longer wishes ptisan to be given, taking care lest the action of the purging drug be weakened.
rendering_2: [354] And since it is prepared in various ways, the version that has taken hellebore but does not contain scammony is the best laxative drug. After the cathartic has been taken it is beneficial to sip ptisane afterwards, as Hippocrates says. For the cathartic drug itself, being small in quantity, arrives at the bottom of the belly, but along its passage the gullet and whatever is high up around the stomach, partaking not only of the quality of the purging agent but also of its substance adhering in the passage, is greatly harmed. The juice of ptisane sipped afterwards is therefore useful, as being able to wash off and sweep downwards what has been plastered on in the passage, and to temper and alter the quality of the drug that has settled into the parts. For these reasons, then, upon the drinking of the cathartic drug he bids one sip ptisane afterwards. But once the purgation has begun to take place, he no longer wishes ptisane to be given, taking care lest the action of the purging drug be dissipated.

greek: δεῖ δὲ [356] ὁμοειδῆ ἀλλήλοις τὰ μιγνύμενα καθαρτικὰ καὶ κατὰ μηδὲν στασιάζειν. ἡ δὲ στάσις αὐτῶν γίνεται, οὐχ ὅταν τὸ μὲν χολῆς, εἰ τύχοι, τὸ δὲ φλέγματος κενωτικὸν, ἀμφότερα γὰρ ἐκκενοῦσθαι δύναται κατὰ τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον, ἀλλ’ ὅταν τὸ μὲν εὐθέως, τὸ δὲ μετὰ πολὺ τῆς προσφορᾶς πεφύκῃ κινεῖν τὴν κάθαρσιν. ἀνώμαλος γὰρ ἡ κένωσις οὕτω γίνεται, προσενεχθέντων ἅμα. λέγω δὲ ἀνώμαλον, ὅταν ἤδη παύεσθαι δοκούσης αὐτῆς ἀρχὴ πάλιν ἑτέρας κενώσεως γίνηται.
rendering_1: It is necessary, moreover, [356] that the cathartics which are mixed together be of like kind with one another and in no respect at variance. Their variance arises not when the one, say, evacuates bile and the other phlegm—for both can be evacuated in the same manner—but when the one is of such a nature as to set the purgation in motion immediately, the other only long after its administration. For in this way the evacuation becomes irregular, when they are administered together. And I call it irregular when, at the point where it already seems to be ceasing, the beginning of another evacuation arises again.
rendering_2: And it is necessary [356] that the cathartics that are mixed be of like kind with one another and in no respect at variance. Their discord arises not when the one, say, evacuates bile and the other phlegm (for both can be evacuated in the same manner), but when the one naturally sets the purgation in motion at once, and the other long after its administration. For in this way the evacuation becomes irregular, when they are administered together. I call it irregular when, while it already seems to be ceasing, the beginning of another evacuation occurs again.

greek: γέγραπται δὲ κατὰ τοὺς Ἱπποκράτους ἀφορισμοὺς περὶ τῶν ὡρῶν· θέρεος φαρμακεύειν ﻿ [348] τὰς ἄνω κοιλίας, χειμῶνος δὲ τὰς κάτω. τὸ δὲ ἀνάλογον ταῖς ὥραις ἐπὶ τῶν χωρῶν σκοπεῖσθαι χρὴ, θερμότητί τε καὶ ψυχρότητι διαιρουμένους· οὕτω δὲ κᾀπὶ τῶν ἡλικιῶν. καὶ μὴν καὶ τὸ ἔθος οὐ σμικρὰ μοῖρα πρὸς ἔνδειξιν κενώσεως. οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἐμεῖν εἰθισμένοι φέρουσιν ἀλυπότερον τὰς διὰ τῆς ἄνω κοιλίας καθάρσεις, οἱ δὲ ἀήθεις οὐκ ἄνευ κινδύνου, καὶ μᾶλλον ἐπὶ ἑλλεβόρου. καὶ τὸ τοῦ νοσήματος δὲ εἶδος σκοπεῖσθαι προσήκει. ἐπὶ μὲν γὰρ τοῦ φλεγματίου ὑδέρου φλέγματος ἀγωγῷ δεῖσθαι τῷ φαρμάκῳ πρότερον μὲν διὰ τῆς κάτω γαστρὸς, εἶτα δι’ ἐμέτων, εἶτα δι’ ἀποφλεγματισμῶν. δι’ ὅλου γὰρ τοῦ σώματος ἐκτεταμένου τοῦ πλεονάζοντος ἁπάσας κενώσεις παραληψόμεθα. ἐπὶ δὲ τοῦ ἀσκίτου ὑδέρου τῶν ὑδραγωγῶν τι δώσομεν φαρμάκων, ὥσπερ γε κᾀπὶ τῶν ἰκτερικῶν τῶν χολαγωγῶν. ἐκκαθαίρειν δὲ χρὴ καὶ τούτων πολυειδῶς τὴν χολὴν ἄνω τε καὶ κάτω καὶ διὰ οὔρων καὶ ὑπερώας καὶ διὰ ῥινῶν.
rendering_1: It is written in the Aphorisms of Hippocrates concerning the seasons: in summer purge [348] the upper cavities, in winter the lower. And what is analogous to the seasons must be considered in the case of regions, dividing them by heat and cold; and so too in the case of ages. And indeed habit also is no small part in the indication of evacuation. For those accustomed to vomit bear with less distress the purgations through the upper cavity, whereas those unaccustomed bear them not without danger, and more so in the case of hellebore. And it is fitting to consider also the form of the disease. For in the case of the phlegmatic dropsy one needs a drug that is a drawer of phlegm, first through the lower belly, then through vomits, then through apophlegmatisms; for since what is in excess is extended throughout the whole body, we shall employ all the evacuations. But in the case of the ascitic dropsy we shall give one of the hydragogue drugs, just as in the case of the icteric one of the cholagogue drugs. And one must purge out the bile of these too in many ways, both upward and downward, and through the urine and the palate and through the nostrils.
rendering_2: It is written in the Aphorisms of Hippocrates concerning the seasons: 'In summer purge [348] the upper cavities, in winter the lower.' And one must consider what corresponds to the seasons in the case of regions, distinguishing them by heat and coldness; and so too in the case of the ages. Moreover, habit is no small factor in the indication for evacuation. For those accustomed to vomiting bear purgations through the upper belly with less distress, whereas the unaccustomed do so not without danger, and more so with hellebore. One ought also to consider the form of the disease. For in phlegmatic dropsy there is need of a drug that draws off phlegm, first through the lower belly, then by vomiting, then by apophlegmatisms. For since what is in excess is spread through the whole body, we shall employ all the evacuations. In ascitic dropsy we shall give one of the water-drawing drugs, just as in jaundiced patients one of the bile-drawing drugs. And in these too one must purge out the bile in many ways, upward and downward, and through the urine and the palate, and through the nostrils.

greek: οὕτω δὲ κᾂν ὁ μελαγχολικὸς πλεονάσῃ χυμὸς, ὡς ἐν μελαγχολίᾳ καὶ καρκίνῳ καὶ [349] ἐλέφαντι, τὸ τῆς μελαίνης χολῆς κενωτικὸν φάρμακον διδόαμεν, ἐπιληψίας δὲ φλεγμαγωγοῖς καθαίρομεν. ἐξ ὧν δῆλον ὅτι ἡ κατάστασις τῆς νόσου καὶ τὸν κενωθησόμενον δηλοῖ χυμὸν καὶ τὸν τόπον δι’ οὗ χρὴ κενοῦν αὐτόν. ἀμέλει καὶ τῶν κατὰ τὸ ἧπαρ φλεγμαινόντων, ὅταν πεφθῶσι, τὴν ἀποκάθαρσιν ποιούμεθα· διὰ μὲν τῆς κάτω γαστρὸς, ὅταν ἐν τοῖς σιμοῖς αὐτοῦ γίνηται τὸ πάθημα, δι’ οὔρων δὲ ὅταν ἐν τοῖς κυρτοῖς. οὕτω δὲ κᾀπὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἐπισκέψῃ, τόν τε πλεονάζοντα χυμὸν καὶ τὸν πεπονθότα τόπον, ἐξ οὗ καθάπερ αἰτίας ὁρμᾶται τὸ νόσημα. ταῦτα γάρ σοι καὶ τὸν κενωθησόμενον ἐνδείξεται χυμὸν καὶ τὸν τρόπον τῆς κενώσεως καὶ τὸν τόπον δι’ οὗ χρὴ κενοῦσθαι, καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἅπασι τὸν καιρόν. ἐν ἀρχῇ μὲν γὰρ τοὺς ὀῤῥώδεις τε καὶ λεπτοὺς κενώσεις χυμούς. ἀναμενεῖς δὲ πέψιν ἐπὶ τῶν παχέων καὶ γλίσχρων, οἷοι τὴν φύσιν εἰσὶν ὅ τε τοῦ φλέγματος καὶ ὁ τῆς μελαίνης χολῆς.
rendering_1: So too, if the melancholic humour is in excess, as in melancholia and cancer and [349] elephas, we give the drug that evacuates black bile, while we purge epilepsies with phlegm-drawing drugs. From which it is clear that the condition of the disease indicates both the humour to be evacuated and the place through which one must evacuate it. Indeed, in the case of those with inflammation in the liver too, once they have been concocted, we carry out the evacuation: through the lower belly, when the affection arises in its concave parts, and through urine, when in its convex parts. So too in the other cases you will examine both the humour that is in excess and the affected place, from which, as from a cause, the disease sets out. For these will indicate to you both the humour to be evacuated and the manner of the evacuation and the place through which it must be evacuated, and, in addition to all these, the right moment. For at the beginning you will evacuate the serous and thin humours; but you will await concoction in the case of the thick and viscous ones, such as by nature are the humour of phlegm and that of black bile.
rendering_2: So too, if the melancholic humour is in excess, as in melancholia, cancer and [349] elephantiasis, we give the drug that evacuates black bile; and cases of epilepsy we purge with phlegm-drawing drugs. From this it is clear that the state of the disease indicates both the humour that is to be evacuated and the place through which one must evacuate it. Indeed, with inflammations in the liver as well, once they have been concocted, we carry out the purging: through the lower belly when the affection arises in its concave parts, and through the urine when it is in the convex parts. In the same way you will examine, in the other cases too, both the humour that is in excess and the affected place, from which, as from a cause, the disease takes its start. For these will indicate to you the humour to be evacuated, the manner of the evacuation, the place through which the evacuation must be made, and, in addition to all these, the right moment. At the beginning you will evacuate the serous and thin humours. But you will wait for concoction in the case of the thick and viscous ones, which is the nature of the humour of phlegm and that of black bile.

greek: ἀλλ’ ἔν γε τοῖς ὀξέσι νοσήμασι κατ’ ἀρχὰς εὐθὺς, ἤτοι κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἡμέραν, ἢ οὐκ ἐξωτέρω τῆς δευτέρας, μέλλοντων ἡμῶν χρῆσθαι [352] ταῖς καθάρσεσιν ὅταν ὀργᾷ, τὴν τοιαύτην παρασκευὴν οὐκ ἐγχωρεῖ γενέσθαι, πλὴν εἰ ἄρα σχοίη τις καιρὸν μελίκρατον ἄκρατον δοῦναι ποιεῖν, ἐναφεψήσας ὑσσώπου τι ἢ θύμου, ἢ ὀριγάνου, ἢ τραγοριγάνου, ἢ γλήχωνος, ἤ τινος τῶν οὕτω λεπτυνόντων, ὥστ’ εὐλόγως ὀλιγάκις ἐν τοῖς ὀξέσιν νοσήμασι κατ’ ἀρχὰς γενήσεται ἡμῖν χρεία φαρμάκων, τῷ μήτε πολλάκις ὀργᾷν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοὺς λυποῦντας, μήτε εἰ καὶ τοῦτο ὑπάρχει, τοῦ νοσοῦντος ἂν ἐπιτηδείου πρὸς τὴν κάθαρσιν ὄντος, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν παρέχοντος ἐπιτήδειον παρασκευάσαι. ὀργᾷν δ’ οἱ χυμοὶ λέγονται, ὅταν ἐν κινήσει σφοδροτέρᾳ γενόμενοι καὶ μεταῤῥέοντες ἀπὸ μορίων εἰς μόρια, κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ νοσήματος ὀχλῶσι τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἀλγοῦντες καὶ ἀσῶντες καὶ γαργαρίζοντες καὶ ἡσυχάζειν οὐκ ἐπιτρέποντες. τοὺς οὖν τοιούτους ἐκκενοῦν προσήκει, τουτέστι τοὺς ἐν κινήσει καὶ φορᾷ καὶ ῥύσει. τοὺς δὲ ἤδη καθ’ ἕν τι μόριον ἐστηριγμένους, οὔτ’ ἄλλῳ τινὶ βοηθήματι χρὴ κινεῖν, οὔτε φαρμακεύειν πρὶν πεφθῆναι. τηνικαῦτα γὰρ καὶ τὴν φύσιν ἕξομεν βοηθοῦσαν τῇ κενώσει.
rendering_1: But in acute diseases, right at the outset, that is, on the first day or not later than the second, when we intend to employ [352] purgations because the humours are turgid, such preparation cannot take place. The exception is if one should perhaps have the opportunity to give unmixed honey-water to be made, with some hyssop or thyme or origanum or goat's origanum or pennyroyal boiled in it, or some other of the things that attenuate in this way. So it is reasonable that in acute diseases we shall seldom have need of drugs at the outset. For the offending humours are not often turgid at the beginning, nor, even if this is the case, would the patient be suited to purgation; indeed he does not even afford us a suitable opportunity to prepare him. The humours are said to be turgid when, having come into more violent motion and flowing over from part to part, they trouble the person at the beginning of the disease, causing pain, causing nausea, gurgling, and not allowing him to keep at rest. Such humours, then, it is proper to evacuate, that is, those in motion, transport and flux. But those already fixed in some one part one must neither stir with any other remedy nor purge with drugs before they have been concocted. For at that time we shall also have nature assisting the evacuation.
rendering_2: But in acute diseases, right at the beginning—that is, on the first day, or not beyond the second—when we are going to employ [352] purgations at the time the humour is in turgor (ὀργᾷ), such a preparation cannot be carried out, unless perhaps one should have the opportunity to have unmixed melikraton made and given, having boiled in it some hyssop, or thyme, or origanum, or goat's-origanum, or pennyroyal, or some other of the things that thin in this way; so that with good reason we shall seldom have need of drugs at the beginning in acute diseases, because neither are the offending humours often in turgor at the beginning, nor, even if this is the case, would the patient be suited to the purgation, nor indeed does he afford us a suitable opportunity to prepare him. The humours are said to be in turgor when, having come into a more violent motion and flowing across from parts to parts, at the beginning of the disease they trouble the person, causing pain and nausea and tickling irritation and not permitting him to be at rest. Such humours, then, it is fitting to evacuate, that is, those that are in motion and movement and flux. But those already fixed in some one part one must neither set in motion by any other remedy nor purge with drugs before they have been concocted. For then we shall also have nature assisting the evacuation.

greek: οὐκ ἐκκρίνει δ’ ἡ γαστὴρ ἐνίοτε καθαρτηρίου δοθέντος, ἤτοι διὰ τὴν ἰδιότητα [355] τῆς τοῦ κάμνοντος φύσεως ἢ διὰ τὴν βραχύτητα τοῦ δοθέντος φαρμάκου. πολλάκις δὲ καὶ κόπρος ἐσφηνωμένη σκληρὰ κατά τινα τῶν ἐντέρων, ἐκκενωθῆναι δυναμένη διὰ κλυστῆρος, πρὶν δίδοσθαι τὸ καθαῖρον φάρμακον κωλύει τὴν κένωσιν. δύναται δὲ καὶ τῆς φύσεως ἐπὶ οὖρα τὴν ὁρμὴν πεποιημένης τὸ καθαρτικὺν μηδὲν ἀνύειν. ἐνίοτε μὲν ὅταν ἀποτύχῃ καθαίροντα, πρὸς τὸ βλάπτειν μηδὲν τὸ σῶμα καὶ τροφὴ γίνεται τοῦ ζώου, τὰ δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ φθαρτικὸν καὶ δηλητήριον ἐκτρέπεται. πάντων δὲ τῶν καθαιρόντων φαρμάκων κακούντων τὴν γαστέρα καὶ μάλιστα αὐτῆς τὸ στόμα, διὰ τὸ νευρωδέστατον εἶναι καὶ αἰσθητικώτατον ἡ μίξις ἐπενοήθη τῶν εὐωδῶν, ὅπως μὴ μόνη μηδὲ ἀκραιφνὴς ἡ δύναμις αὐτῶν ἅπτεται τοῦ σώματος τῆς γαστρός. χρὴ δὲ εἶναι τὰ μιγνύμενα σπέρματα τοιαῦτα, ἃ καὶ τὴν κακίαν πέφυκεν ἀμβλύνειν καὶ τὴν ἐνέργειαν αὐτῶν μὴ κωλύειν, λεπτυντικῆς τε καὶ τμητικῆς ὄντα δυνάμεως, ὥστε καὶ τοὺς παχεῖς χυμοὺς τέμνειν καὶ τὰς ὁδοὺς αὐτῶν, δι’ ὧν ἐκκενοῦνται, διανοίγειν τε καὶ ἀναστομοῦν.
rendering_1: Sometimes the belly does not evacuate when a purgative has been given, either because of the peculiarity [355] of the patient's nature or because of the smallness of the drug given. Often, too, hard faeces wedged in one of the intestines prevent the evacuation; these can be evacuated by a clyster before the purging drug is given. It is also possible for the cathartic to achieve nothing when nature has directed its impulse towards the urine. Sometimes, when purging drugs fail, not only do they do the body no harm but they even become nourishment for the animal; others, however, turn towards what is destructive and deleterious. Since all purging drugs injure the stomach, and above all its mouth, because it is most nervous and most sensitive, the admixture of fragrant substances was devised, so that their power should not touch the body of the stomach alone and unmixed. The seeds that are mixed in must be such as naturally both blunt their harmfulness and do not hinder their action, being of a thinning and cutting power, so as both to cut the thick humours and to open up and unstop the passages through which they are evacuated.
rendering_2: Sometimes, however, the belly does not excrete when a purgative has been given, either because of the peculiarity [355] of the patient's nature or because of the smallness of the quantity of the drug given. Often, too, hard faeces wedged in one of the intestines, which could have been evacuated by means of a clyster before the purging drug was given, prevents the evacuation. It is also possible that, when the nature has directed its impulse toward the urine, the cathartic accomplishes nothing. Sometimes, when purging drugs fail, some of them, besides doing no harm at all to the body, even become nourishment for the living being, while others turn toward the destructive and poisonous. And since all purging drugs harm the belly, and especially its mouth, because it is most sinewy and most sensitive, the admixture of fragrant substances was devised, so that their power might not touch the body of the belly alone and unmixed. The seeds that are mixed in must be such as are naturally able both to blunt their harmfulness and not to hinder their activity, being of an attenuating and incisive power, so as both to cut the thick humours and to open up and unstop the passages through which they are evacuated.

greek: χρὴ δὲ προλεπτύνειν καὶ τέμνειν τοὺς παχεῖς χυμοὺς καὶ γλίσχρους καὶ τοὺς πόρους δι’ ὧν οὗτοι μεταλαμβάνονταί τε καὶ ἕλκονται πρὸ τῶν καθαρτικῶν φαρμάκων ἀναστομοῦν, εἰ ἡ [346] κάθαρσις ἀρίστη μέλλει γίνεσθαι κατὰ πάντα καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῶν ἑλλέβορον λαμβανόντων. ἡ γὰρ συντονία τῶν σπαραγμῶν ἐκβάλλουσα τοὺς ἐσφηνωμένους δυσλύτως τοῖς πεπονθόσι μέρεσι χυμοὺς καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο τὰ χρόνια τῶν παθῶν ὠφελοῦσα, ῥᾷον ἀπεργάσεται τοῦτο προλελεπτυσμένων αὐτῶν. εἰ δὲ ἀμελήσουσι τούτων, δυσχερεῖς ἀπαντῶσιν αἱ καθάρσεις, μετὰ στρόφων ἐνίοτε καί τινων ἰλίγγων, ἄσης τε πολλῆς καὶ κακοσφυξίας, ἐκλύσεώς τε καὶ δυσκολίας. τοὺς μέλλοντας δὲ ἑλλέβορον λήψεσθαι προπειρᾶσθαι χρὴ τῆς φύσεως, ὅπως ἔχῃ πρὸς τὰς ἄνω καθάρσεις, τουτέστι τὰς δι’ ἐμέτων. γενέσθω δὲ ἡ πεῖρα διὰ τῶν ἐμετικῶν φαρμάκων, ὅσα μέτρια. ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ ῥᾳδίως φαί νηται καθαιρόμενος, οὐ χρὴ τὸν τοιοῦτον ἄνθρωπον ἐπὶ τὸν ἑλλέβορον ἄγειν, ἄνευ τοῦ προπαρασκευάσαι. γένοιτο δ’ ἂν τοῦτο καὶ δι’ αὐτῶν καὶ συνεχῶν ἐμέτων, ἐθισθέντος ἑτοίμως ἐμεῖν τοῦ ληψομένου τὸν ἑλλέβορον. γένοιτο δ’ ἂν ἄμεινον καὶ διὰ τοῦ προϋγρᾶναι τὰ σώματα. προϋγραίνεται δὲ πλείονι τροφῇ καὶ ἀναπαύσει.
rendering_1: One must first thin and cut the thick and viscous humours, and open up the passages through which these are transferred and drawn, before the cathartic drugs, if the [346] purgation is to be best in every respect, and especially in the case of those taking hellebore. For the intensity of the convulsive retchings, which expels the humours that are wedged in the affected parts in a manner hard to loosen and in this respect benefits the chronic affections, will accomplish this more easily when they have been thinned beforehand. But if they neglect these things, the purgations turn out troublesome, sometimes accompanied by gripings and certain vertigos, much nausea and bad pulse, faintness and distress. In those who are about to take hellebore, one must first make trial of their nature, to see how it stands with regard to upward purgations, that is, those through vomiting. Let the trial be made by means of emetic drugs, such as are moderate. For if he does not appear to be purged easily, one must not lead such a person on to hellebore without preparing him beforehand. This could be done both through these very [emetics] and through repeated vomitings, the person who is going to take the hellebore being habituated to vomit readily. And it would be done better also by moistening the bodies beforehand. They are moistened beforehand by more abundant nourishment and by rest.

But if they neglect these things, the purgations turn out troublesome, sometimes with gripings and some vertigo, much nausea and bad pulse, faintness and discomfort. In those who are about to take hellebore one must first test the nature, how it stands with regard to purgations upwards, that is, those by vomiting. For if he does not appear to be purged easily, one ought not to bring such a person to hellebore without preparing him beforehand. This could be done both by these themselves and by continual vomitings, the person who is going to take the hellebore having been accustomed to vomit readily. And it could be done better also by moistening the bodies beforehand. They are moistened beforehand by more abundant food and by rest.
